figures.caption: Fig. 4: Persistence predictions for two object classes, each in a moving and stationary context: a cutting board being washed (a) vs. resting on the counter (b), and a car in a driving lane (c) vs. in a parking spot (d). The instance masks are shown in green. The table reports each method’s predicted persistence interval [q25, q75], with each cell shaded by its predicted duration (darker = longer).

Fig. 2: The two PreSIST predictor instantiations. PreSIST-Lang (top) issues two vision-language model queries to caption image I and describe each instance from I plus two object detail views of mask M ; given these outputs, a language model produces survival-time quantiles (q25, q75). PreSIST-Vis (bottom) encodes I into patch tokens, mask-pools them under M into an object query that cross-attends to the patch tokens and regresses the quantiles. In training, PreSIST-Lang quantiles become log-space targets (z1, z2) for loss L. Dotted inputs and outputs mark connections to the overall pipeline (Fig. 1).
Fig. 3: Zero-shot persistence prediction MAE over varying prediction horizons across all evaluation domains; lower is better.
